$meta.name: Travel app design tokens - sprint 9 additions
$meta.status: Draft for Raz. DELTA ONLY on top of 0.9.0: every key below is new; no existing value changes. No new hex value: the discovery colour reuses color.region.urban / color.dark.region.urban. Merge into docs/design/tokens.json and apps/mobile/src/theme/tokens.ts in the same PR that first uses them (docs/design/sprint-09/README.md section 18). Keys starting with '$check.' are contrast documentation only and are not merged into tokens.ts.
globe.final.discover.color.note: Same value as color.dark.region.urban. The globe scene is always space (globe.status), so one value serves both themes. Differs from selection (highlightColor #FF7A57) by hue and from trips (globe.final.trips.color #4FCFBE) by hue; trips and discover have almost the same luminance (1.13:1), which is why the trip layers are hidden while discovery is active (README 5.3).
globe.final.discover.dim.note: A fill over every land feature that does not match, including Israel, Antarctica, Gaza and areas without an adm0 code. The ocean is never dimmed (README 6).
globe.final.discover.note: Layer opacity fades only when discovery starts or is cleared. A country joining or leaving the result is instant: one 'in' filter on the adm0 list per layer, as the trip highlight (ADR-014 D4), AC-11 500 ms. Layer order: trips < dim < discover fill/line < discover rings < selection highlight. While the mode is on the trip layers' opacity is 0 (README 5.3). Reduced motion: 0 for both (as the selection highlight).
globe.final.cityPin.note: Circle layers only, no new image. strokeColor = highlightColor (the pin belongs to the selected country). Drawn above the selection outline. Removed on Clear, on a new search, or when the card closes (AC-13).
color.discover.swatch.note: Decorative legend dot in the results panel header and rows, tying the list to the globe colour. Same values as color.region.urban / color.dark.region.urban. Never the only carrier of meaning.
color.discover.chipOnGlobe.map: No new colours. Off: color.<scheme>.chrome.bg / chrome.fg / chrome.border (as ChromeButton). On: color.dark.action.primary.bg (#6FB3FA) and color.dark.action.primary.fg (#060B18) in BOTH themes, because the globe is always dark (same reasoning as the SOS button). Disabled: color.<scheme>.action.disabled.bg / fg.
color.discover.whyChip.map: No new colours. bg.tag + text.primary. Deliberately neutral, not status.success: a green 'Advisory level 2' would read as 'safe' (spec 5.12: no 'safe' or 'recommended').
layout.discover.note: Offsets below insets.top. chipsTop = layout.chrome.rowTop (52) + 48 + 8. refineTop = chipsTop + 48. Toasts and the globe error banner move to overlayTop.oneRow / .twoRows while the rows are visible (README 2.1).
layout.discover.panel.note: Non-modal panel in the globe screen's tree (not BottomSheet, which is a Modal with a scrim and would hide the painted globe). Two heights: open = min(content, maxRatio * window height); collapsed = peek (handle + count header) + insets.bottom. No snap library (README 8.9).
motion.discover.note: announceDelay = motion.search.announceDelay. homeEase is a proposal (README 14): when discovery starts at the whole-globe view, ease the centre to 35E 25N so Israel's neighbourhood faces the user. Reduced motion: every movement becomes a fade or 0; the paint and the list are never delayed by animation (AC-11).
rules.discover.note: NOT tokens (business rules, kept in discover.ts next to its case table; ADR-014): family 12 <= t <= 30 in the picker's month; hot t >= 24 and wet <= 8 and coastline (CIA landlocked list); pleasant 16 <= t < 24 and wet <= 10; cool 0 < t < 16; winter t <= 0; t is the displayed whole-degree value, wet whole days; hours = km from Ben Gurion (34.8867, 32.0114) / 800 + 0.5, rounded to the half hour with ties up, filtered after rounding; near <= 5 h; cities >= 100k population, up to 3 listed by population.
$check.contrast.method: WCAG 2.x relative luminance, (L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05), on the hex values. Text 4.5:1, graphics 3:1 (1.4.11).
$check.contrast.discover #B896F5 vs trip: 1.13 - same luminance, hue only: trips hidden in discovery mode
$check.contrast.discover #B896F5 vs sele: different hue (270 vs 14 degrees); the selection keeps its white outline, so it never relies on hue alone
$check.contrast.light primary #1561BC vs: 1.97 FAIL - reason the 'on' chip always uses the dark primary pair
$check.contrast.disabled chip action.dis: 4.35 light / 4.15 dark - disabled controls are exempt (1.4.3); the explanation is a Toast in normal text
